name: Nitrogen
occurrence: Makes up 78% of Earth's atmosphere as inert diatomic N₂ gas.
biologicalRelevance: Essential to every amino acid and nucleotide base — proteins and DNA cannot exist without it, and its fixation from the atmosphere is a bottleneck for all life.
notableCharacteristics: The N≡N triple bond in N₂ gas is one of the strongest bonds known, which is exactly why atmospheric nitrogen is so hard to 'fix' into usable compounds.
whyHere: Five valence electrons let it form a very stable triple bond as N₂, which explains both why it dominates the atmosphere unreactively and why converting it into ammonia industrially needs high pressure, heat, and a catalyst.
didYouKnow: Despite being 78% of the air you breathe, nitrogen gas is so unreactive that most living things can't use it directly — they depend on bacteria that can break that triple bond.
genZNote: 78% of the air, 0% of the drama. Too stable to react with anything until industrial chemistry forces the issue.
